Watch a Bot use its browser and tools, answer with interactive results, and wait for your approval before it sends. Take over when it needs you, and connect the agents you already run.

## Getting started ### On your laptop The easiest way to get started is with the fully self-contained app that runs on your laptop, combining the OpenBot frontend and Docker-based backend in one application. [Mac / Apple silicon](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-mac-arm64.dmg) · [Mac / Intel](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-mac-x64.dmg) · [Windows](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-windows-x64-setup.exe) [Run from source](#run-from-source) ### For your team **OpenBot for Business** brings your agents into one workspace with company sign-in, tool permissions, approvals, and audit. Deploy on your infrastructure or work with our engineers on hosting and customization. [**Get early access to OpenBot for Business →**](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=business&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [**Talk to an engineer**](https://open.bot/business) · [**Kubernetes setup**](#deploy-on-kubernetes) ### Web, mobile, and chat [Web](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=web&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [iOS](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=ios&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Android](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=android&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Slack](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=slack&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Teams](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=teams&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) ## Your workspace. Your stack.
- **Choose your models.** Use OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, or open models through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, hosted by a provider or on your own infrastructure. Keep your provider relationships and change models as your needs change. - **Bring your agents.** Run built-in Bots in the OpenBot server, or connect your existing agents through AG-UI from any agent execution platform. Agents built with different stacks can work in the same workspace. - **Make it yours.** Use the MIT-licensed template as-is, white-label it, or customize it deeply. AG-UI connects agents, MCP connects tools, and the frontends and backend can evolve independently. - **Govern work across your team.** Company sign-in, roles, tool permissions, approvals, and audit apply across the workspace. Your agents use OpenBot's tools and computers under the same policies. - **Get help deploying it.** CopilotKit's engineers can work with your team to deploy OpenBot, connect your systems, and automate parts of specific jobs. [Connect your agent](#bring-your-own-agent) · [Configure models and tools](docs/configuration.md) · [Explore OpenBot for Business](https://open.bot/business) ## Built on CopilotKit and AG-UI OpenBot is built on [CopilotKit](https://www.copilotkit.ai), which is [used in production by a majority of Fortune 500 companies](https://www.copilotkit.ai/blog/series-a). **Your agent stack.** [AG-UI](https://docs.ag-ui.com/introduction#supported-integrations) has first-class integrations across the major agent frameworks and harnesses, including Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK, Microsoft Agent Framework and Agent Harness, Google ADK, AWS Strands, Oracle Agent Spec, LangChain, Mastra, Pydantic AI, Agno, and CrewAI. Many ship first-party support; [Amazon Bedrock AgentCore supports AG-UI directly](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-agui.html). **Your execution platform.** Keep your agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Claude Managed Agents, [Google's Agent Platform](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform), LangChain's Managed Deep Agents, [Microsoft Foundry Agent Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agents), or your own infrastructure. Connect them to OpenBot through an AG-UI endpoint, using an adapter where needed. Your choice of agent platform stays independent of your workspace. ## Architecture OpenBot has three parts. On your laptop, setup runs the backend and Intelligence for you. For a team, the Helm charts deploy both on Kubernetes in your own infrastructure: `openbot-bundle` installs the two together, and `openbot` installs OpenBot beside an Intelligence that already runs. | Part | What it does | | --- | --- | | **OpenBot frontends** | Mac, Windows, web, iOS, Android, Slack, and Teams connect people to the same workspace. Conversations, interactive results, computer view, and approvals adapt to each surface. [Choose a frontend](#getting-started). | | **OpenBot backend** | Runs the workspace API and built-in Bots, connects external agents and tools, manages Bot computers, and enforces identity, permissions, action policies, and audit. Published as signed images and Helm charts, and reached through [one API](#api). Deploys on Kubernetes with PostgreSQL and persistent storage. | | **CopilotKit Intelligence** | Durable conversations, memory, Automatic Learning, and enterprise governance services. Separately licensed; runs on Kubernetes alongside OpenBot. | OpenBot enforces sign-in, tool permissions, action policies, and audit at its API, alongside Intelligence's platform services. Built-in Bots run in the OpenBot server; your own agents can run alongside OpenBot or on any agent execution platform. Both use AG-UI and can share the same workspace. Computer execution is pluggable: use the default Kubernetes setup or connect a compatible external computer provider. [Architecture details](docs/architecture.md) · [Services and ports](#services-and-ports) · [Kubernetes deployment](#deploy-on-kubernetes) ## Open source, local operation, and licensing **The OpenBot application template is open source under the [MIT license](LICENSE).** You can fork, modify, and white-label it. It uses **CopilotKit Intelligence**, which is separately licensed and can run entirely on your own machine or infrastructure. | Where you run it | CopilotKit Intelligence license | | --- | --- | | **Your laptop, for personal use and experimentation** | Requires a free local Intelligence license. Desktop setup handles this for you. | | **Kubernetes evaluation** | Requires a free Intelligence trial license. [Request a trial](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=business&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access). | | **Kubernetes / production** | Requires a production Intelligence license beyond evaluation. OpenBot for Business includes Intelligence for use with OpenBot. [Plans and pricing](https://open.bot/pricing). | **Fully local is an option.** Run OpenBot, Intelligence, and a compatible model locally. A cloud model or connected online app still sends requests to that service. Initial downloads, account sign-in, and local license renewal need internet access. --- ## Deploy on Kubernetes Deploy OpenBot on **AWS EKS, Azure AKS, Google GKE, or your own Kubernetes cluster**. Each release publishes two Helm charts: | Chart | What it installs | | --- | --- | | **`openbot-bundle`** (`openbot-bundle-0.1.0.tgz` in v1.1.0) | OpenBot and CopilotKit Intelligence together, on one PostgreSQL server. Nobody signs in to Intelligence: the chart makes OpenBot's organization, project and key in it. The quickest way to try OpenBot on a cluster, and the evaluation below. | | **`openbot`** (`openbot-0.3.0.tgz` in v1.1.0) | OpenBot alone, pointed at an Intelligence that already runs, managed or self-hosted: its two addresses in `config.intelligence.apiUrl` and `config.intelligence.gatewayWsUrl`, and a project key. | For a first evaluation, you need a cluster with a **default StorageClass**, `kubectl`, Helm, a **trial or production license**, and a model key. The install requests about 3.15 vCPU while it runs, plus about 0.4 vCPU while its install Jobs run; on EKS that is three t3.large nodes, not two. The commands below use an OpenAI key. For Anthropic, a model router, your own database, or OpenBot against an Intelligence you already run, use the Helm guide that comes with each chart (`helm show readme` on the chart). > **Setting up with an AI assistant?** Give it this README and the Helm guide (`helm show readme` on the chart below). The guide covers cloud-specific values, storage, secrets, sign-in, networking, upgrades, and troubleshooting. Use the evaluation below only through a local port-forward; configure sign-in and TLS before sharing a deployment. 1. **Create `openbot-values.yaml` locally.** Replace the placeholders with your license and model key. Keep this file out of source control. ```yaml openbot: config: singleUser: true secrets: licenseToken: "" modelApiKey: "" ``` 2. **Install** the `openbot-bundle` chart published with the release. ```sh helm install openbot https://github.com/CopilotKit/OpenBot/releases/download/v1.1.0/openbot-bundle-0.1.0.tgz \ --namespace openbot --create-namespace \ --values openbot-values.yaml \ --timeout 15m ``` On arm64 nodes, add `--set intelligence.embeddings.enabled=false`. The OpenBot image runs on amd64 and arm64, but the embeddings server Intelligence runs for Memory is amd64 only. Without it, Memory recalls by keyword. 3. **Open your evaluation.** ```sh kubectl -n openbot get pods,jobs kubectl -n openbot port-forward svc/openbot-server 3001:3001 ``` Open . This configuration is single-user: anyone who can reach it is an administrator. Keep the port-forward local. The chart generates every password, key and token both products need, creates both databases, and sets up Intelligence's organization, OpenBot's project and the Learning container. OpenBot's server migrates its own database as it starts and does the scheduled work itself, so there is no migration Job and no CronJob. Automatic Learning uses your model key too. For OpenBot against managed Intelligence, or an Intelligence you already run, install the `openbot` chart instead (`https://github.com/CopilotKit/OpenBot/releases/download/v1.1.0/openbot-0.3.0.tgz`) with `config.intelligence.apiUrl`, `config.intelligence.gatewayWsUrl` and `secrets.intelligenceApiKey`; its guide has the commands. A release of the 0.2 chart that still runs the Intelligence it installed is refused at upgrade to 0.3: keep it on 0.2, or install `openbot-bundle` as a new release in a namespace of its own. For a team deployment, follow the Helm guide (`helm show readme` on the chart) to configure authentication, TLS, your database, secrets, persistent storage, and network policies. For a single-container alternative, see [Deploy it](#deploy-it). ## Run from source Use the template to customize the workspace, branding, Bots, and skills. The source setup below uses [an Intelligence on your own machine](#intelligence-on-your-own-machine) by default; managed Intelligence is the alternative. ```sh git clone https://github.com/CopilotKit/OpenBot.git cd OpenBot ``` ### Requirements To run the open-source template locally, you’ll need the following. - Docker, for PostgreSQL, the API server and the shipped Bots. The server and the Bots' computers run from the published OpenBot images, which `scripts/start.sh` pulls at the tag in `backend-images.env`: `main` in a checkout of `main`, the images built from main, and the release's own version in a release (`v1.0.3` in the v1.0.3 tag). Nothing else is built or needed for them. - [Bun](https://bun.sh) 1.4+, for the app, the setup helpers and the tests (some tests fail on 1.3). - A CopilotKit account, for CopilotKit Intelligence. The free plan covers an Intelligence on your own machine and a managed project. - A model key. The example configuration uses OpenAI; Anthropic and Google work too, with `BOT_PROVIDER` set. ### Quick start The example configuration sets `OPENBOT_SINGLE_USER=true`, so you can try the app as a local administrator. Configure [sign-in](#sign-in) before giving anyone else access. > **Setting up with an AI assistant?** Paste [`prompt.txt`](prompt.txt) into it first. It carries the > same steps as below plus the things that are easy to get wrong: which of the blank keys in > `.env.example` are actually yours to fill (the CopilotKit key and a model key), which the start > script fills for you, and what each start-up refusal means. Every claim in it is checked against > this repository. 1. Create `.env`: ```sh cp .env.example .env bun install ``` 2. Connect Intelligence. `.env.example` leaves its two addresses and its key empty, for one of these to fill. **On this machine**, the default (a preview for macOS with Docker Desktop; see [Intelligence on your own machine](#intelligence-on-your-own-machine)): ```sh npx --yes copilotkit@latest login npx --yes copilotkit@latest local setup npx --yes copilotkit@latest local connect --approve-connection ``` `local setup` installs
